(Per: The Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Vijaykumar A.Patil)

This appeal is filed by the injured claimant seeking higher compensation being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 17.01.2019 passed in M.V.C. No.345/2017 by the Senior Civil Judge & Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-X,
Hungund (for short, 'the Tribunal).
2. Brief facts of the case are that the petitioner in the instant claim petition and the claimant in MVC No.346/2017 were proceeding on motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-29/R-3600, as rider and pillion rider, and at that time a TATA ACE vehicle bearing registration No.KA-25/C-8555 came and dashed against the motor NC: 2024:KHC-D:12981-DB cycle, as a result of which, both of them sustained grievous injuries all over body.

Hungund
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: On a claim petition-MVC No.345/2017 being filed by the appellant/claimant seeking compensation for the injuries suffered by him, notices were issued and the claim petition was contested by respondent No.2-insurance company.

The Tribunal on the basis of the oral and documentary evidence placed before it, held that both rider of the motor cycle and the driver of TATA ACE vehicle were equally responsible for the accident, and as such, while assessing the total compensation at Rs.2,00,200/-, the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.1,00,100/- to the appellant with interest at the rate of 7% per annum from the date of petition till realization. Being aggrieved by the same, the appellant/claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: 2 3. Sri. Anand R.Kolli, learned counsel for the appellant/claimant, submits that the Tribunal committed a grave error in assessing the income of the injured at NC: 2024:KHC-D:12981-DB Rs.9,000/- per month, and prays for reassessing the income on higher side.
He also submits that the Tribunal erred in assessing the disability at 5% since the doctor has assessed the disability at 35% to particular limb and 15% to the whole body.
He further submits that the compensation awarded under other heads is on the lower side and prays that the same be enhanced appropriately.
Thus, he seeks to allow the appeal and grant higher compensation.

4. Per contra, Sri. Nagaraj C.Kolloori, learned counsel, appearing for respondent No.2-insurance company supports the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal and submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on all heads is just and proper and the same needs no interference by this Court.
Thus, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.
5. We have heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for respondent No.2- insurance company, and perused the appeal papers.
The appellant/claimant claimed that he was doing electrical work and earning a sum of Rs.10,000/- per month.
However, claimant had not produced any cogent evidence to prove his avocation and income.
In the absence of any cogent evidence, the Tribunal has assessed the income of the claimant at Rs.9,000/- per month which is just and proper and no interference is called for by this Court.

The doctor-P.W.3 has assessed the permanent disability suffered by the appellant at 35%
to particular limb and 15% to the whole body.
The Tribunal has assessed the whole body disability at 5% which, in our view, is on the lower side and we deem it appropriate to reassess the disability at 8%.

The appropriate multiplier applicable is '18' having regard to the age of the appellant/claimant,
who was aged 23 years as on the date of the accident.

Since the disability is reassessed at 8%, the appellant/claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,55,520/- [Rs.9,000 x 8% x 12 x 18].
NC: 2024:KHC-D:12981-DB 7.

Having regard to the injuries suffered by the appellant/claimant, the period of hospitalization and the treatment taken by him, we deem it appropriate to enhance the compensation under the head 'pain & suffering' to Rs.40,000/-; Rs.30,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'; and Rs.15,000/- towards attendant charges, food & nourishment and transportation and incidental charges.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards medical expenses is left unaltered.
The compensation towards loss of income during laid up period is enhanced to Rs.27,000/- taking the laid up period as three months.

8. On re-assessment, the claimant is entitled to a total compensation as under:
1. Pain & suffering Rs. 40,000/-
2.

Medical expenses Rs. 70,000/-

Insofar as the finding of the Tribunal with holding both the rider of the motor cycle and the driver of the TATA ACE vehicle negligent in causing the accident to the extent of 50% is concerned
, on perusal of the impugned judgment we affirm the said finding.
Hence, the appellant/claimant is entitled to Rs.1,68,760/- (being 50% of Rs.3,37,520/-) as against Rs.1,00,100/- awarded by the Tribunal.
The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.

10. In the result, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a) Appeal stands allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the claimant is entitled to total compensation to Rs.1,68,760/- as against Rs.1,00,100/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

c) The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum NC:
2024:KHC-D:12981-DB from the date of petition till the date of payment.
d) The Respondent No.2-insurance company shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from today.
